script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE LAST HUG

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JANE, a successful businesswoman in her mid-forties, sits at a table, sipping her coffee. A phone call interrupts her thoughts. It's her estranged father, JACK, who has been in prison for 20 years.

JANE
(Into the phone)
Dad? Is this some kind of joke?

INT. PRISON VISITING ROOM - DAY

JACK, an elderly man with a weary expression, sits on a bench, waiting for his visit. A guard approaches.

GUARD
(Reading from a list)
Jane Doe, here to see Jack Doe.

Jack stands, looking hopeful. The guard nods, and Jack enters the visiting room, where Jane sits, her expression unchanged.

JACK
(Nervously)
I'm glad you came, Jane. I've got a lot to say to you.

JANE
(Coldly)
What could you possibly have to say that would make this worth my time?

JACK
(Sighs)
I want to ask for your forgiveness, Jane.

JANE
(Angrily)
For what? For abandoning me and my mother when I was just a child? For ruining our lives?

Jack's face falls, and he looks down at his hands.

JACK
Yes, I've done all that. But I was a desperate man, Jane. I made a terrible mistake, and I've spent every day in prison regretting it.

JANE
(Scoffs)
You think a few words can undo the damage you've caused?

JACK
No, I don't. But maybe, just maybe, it's a start.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits on her couch, lost in thought, as she flips through old family photos. She remembers her father's kindness and love before his downward spiral.

JANE
(To herself)
Could I forgive him? Could I let go of the anger and hurt?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane sits at the same table, still contemplating her father's request. Across the room, she sees a man, MIKE, in his late thirties, arguing with a waitress. As the argument escalates, Jane realizes it's her ex-husband.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

Mike storms out of the coffee shop, and Jane approaches the waitress, who is clearly shaken. Jane offers a kind word and a listening ear, and the waitress thanks her.

JANE
(To herself)
Forgiveness isn't always easy, but it's worth the effort.

INT. PRISON VISITING ROOM - DAY

Jane returns to the visiting room, determined to see her father one more time. Jack looks up, surprised but hopeful.

JANE
(Softly)
I've come to give you a chance, Dad. But this is the last hug I can give you.

Jack takes Jane's hand, and they share a long, emotional embrace. Jane finally forgives her father, releasing years of pain and anger.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits on her couch, holding an old family photo. She looks content, her expression gentle and at peace.

JANE
(To herself)
Sometimes, the last hug is the most powerful one of all.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
